# Report - video8, L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (round 001)

Representation level: L1 (simple geometric proxies). This is the Three.js sampled-frame baseline, not a protocol-equivalent Blender reproduction.

## Observed in the 24 reference samples
- One continuous shot (no cuts), 12 s / 360 frames at 30 fps, from the rear seat of a tandem high-wing light aircraft.
- Main subjects: the front-seat pilot (back view: short light-brown hair, pale-green headset, black fleece top, grey-green harness straps), a black shoulder-harness strap hanging from the ceiling between camera and pilot, the cabin (cream ceiling/upper walls, red vent boxes, overhead radio console upper-left, black window frames, overhead skylight with green-tinted frame, tube-braced windscreen, cream instrument panel), and the farmland/sky outside.
- 0-4 s: steep nose-down attitude; ground fills windscreen, side windows and (around 1.5-3.6 s) the skylight. 4-8 s: pull-out; the horizon appears first in the left window and rises, tilted higher on the right (slight right bank) and levels by ~8.8 s. 8.8-12 s: roughly level / slightly nose-up flight, horizon near mid-frame.
- Handheld camera: tilts up and left around 1.5-2.6 s (overhead console and skylight dominant), tilts down ~4-7 s and progressively down again after 9.4 s (seat back visible at the end).
- Pilot turns his head to his left (image left, sunglasses profile visible) from ~9.6 s to ~11 s and back to forward by ~12 s.

## Model
- Cabin built from boxes/cylinders in an aircraft group; the camera is a child of that group (eye at the cabin origin, vertical FOV 70 deg).
- Pilot: hip-pivot group (torso box, shoulder cylinder, collar), articulated head group (skin/hair spheres, sunglasses and nose boxes, headset cups and band) with keyframed head yaw; torso lean keyframed.
- Outside: large ground plane with an in-memory seeded procedural farmland DataTexture (fields, tree lines, woods, creeks, ponds, buildings, roads), linear haze fog, vertex-coloured sky dome.
- Animation: aircraft pitch/bank/heading and camera-in-cabin pitch/yaw are Hermite-interpolated keyframes at the sample timestamps, estimated from horizon height/tilt and from the image positions of the instrument panel and pilot head. Everything is an absolute function of time.

## Inference vs evidence
The attitudes between samples, the heading change during the dive (the ground layout is generic, not matched), the exact lens FOV and cabin dimensions are inferred. No render feedback has been received yet for this initial version.

rounds.reason: Fix strap orientation, pilot torso/head proxies, seat height, console and outdoor colours after round 1 feedback.

# Report - video8, L1 proxy, CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (round 002)

Representation level: L1 (simple geometric proxies). Three.js sampled-frame baseline; not equivalent to Blender model rankings.

## Observed in the 24 reference samples
- One continuous shot (no cuts), 12 s / 360 frames at 30 fps, from the rear seat of a tandem high-wing light aircraft looking forward over the front pilot.
- Subjects: front-seat pilot (back view, light-brown hair, pale-green headset, black fleece, dark harness straps), a black shoulder-harness strap hanging from the ceiling between camera and pilot, the cabin (cream ceiling/upper walls, red vent boxes, overhead radio console upper-left, black window frames, skylight with green frame, tube-braced windscreen, cream instrument panel, front seat back) and the farmland/sky outside.
- 0-4 s steep nose-down attitude (ground in windscreen, side windows and, ~1.5-3.6 s, the skylight); 4-8 s pull-out with the horizon appearing in the left window first and tilted higher on the right (slight right bank); ~8.8-12 s near-level flight with the horizon near mid-frame.
- Handheld camera tilts up/left ~1.5-2.6 s, down ~4-7 s and progressively down after ~9.4 s.
- Pilot turns his head to his left (image left; sunglasses profile) ~9.6-11 s and back to forward by ~12 s.

## Model
- Cabin of boxes/cylinders in an aircraft group; camera child of the cabin (eye at origin, vertical FOV 70 deg).
- Pilot: hip-pivot group (torso box, rounded shoulder cylinder, collar, neck, harness straps) with keyframed lean; head group (hair skull, face, sunglasses, nose, headset cups/band, mic) with keyframed yaw for the head turn.
- Outside: ground plane with an in-memory seeded procedural farmland DataTexture, haze fog, vertex-coloured sky dome.
- Aircraft pitch/bank/heading and camera-in-cabin pitch/yaw are Hermite-interpolated keyframes at the sample times (from horizon height/tilt and panel/head image positions). All state is an absolute function of time.

## Feedback received and revisions
Round 001 render feedback (24 paired frames) showed: horizon height/tilt and overall cabin framing broadly matching; the ceiling strap rendered edge-on (orientation bug), pilot shoulders too high and torso too boxy with oversized bright harness block, front seat back far too high and bright, head reading as a skin ball, overhead console dominated by a dark strip, overly green ground with heavy black creek lines, pale sky. Round 002 fixes the strap orientation/width, lowers and rounds the shoulders, darkens/narrows harness straps, lowers and greys the seat, rebuilds the head (hair skull, face, neck), adds console knobs, removes the skylight centre rib, retunes ground palette and sky gradient, and thins window frames and the coiled cord.

## Remaining uncertainties
Attitudes between samples, heading change during the dive, ground layout (generic, not matched), lens FOV and exact cabin dimensions are inferred; the reference lens distortion is not modelled.

rounds.reason: Add camera roll, refine pull-out horizon, seat/shoulder/panel proportions after round 2 feedback.
